The proposed implementation contract

Preserve positions 1–100 and add 160 missions after them. The first ten zone identities follow the actual environments of the existing route. The remaining sixteen form a new continuation ending in Event Horizon. This avoids inserting unearned missions ahead of established progress or moving the three barriers. All existing mission IDs, modes, targets and objective definitions remain, including the nine Spill assignments. Ten existing flight configurations lose the strobe as requested.

The map stays one ascending road numbered 1 through the published end. Zone names and gradual changes in scenery identify places; players will not see ten-level boxes, chapter tabs, dividing lines or “10/10” zone quotas. Future releases append missions without redefining IDs, seeds, past rewards or completion titles.

Basis: the supplied brief and subsequent instructions, plus main at 7f74b80. No separate earlier proposal attachment was available to read, and its full text was not recovered. This draft does not claim an earlier zone order or reward choice was approved.

Locked constraints: no tap-triggered blackout flashing; no new gameplay mechanics; no changes to the Spill wave ladder, Depot timing, standard mission starting ship, Ore rules, endless continuation or wave-20 first-pass behavior. New Spill ships mean cosmetic finishes on the existing modular ship, and new pals are cosmetic companions. Existing player suit/helmet artwork and animation are outside this work.

What current main actually does

Main was fetched and pinned at 7f74b80, the merge of PR #178 — endless Spill with untimed Depot progression. Both an open-PR search and the open-pulls endpoint returned no open PRs. Relevant recent merged work includes #178 and the shared rendering/cosmetic work in #175 and #173. No AGENTS.md was found in the tracked tree or applicable workspace ancestors; README directs edits to illustrated-src and generation of docs output. No build was run.

The requested files were inspected: campaign.ts, catalog.ts, standalone.ts, sim.ts, save.ts, engine.ts and build-roadmap.mjs. The relevant draw, sky-generation, art-loading, Spill and test paths were also inspected. Runtime probes executed the existing shipped JavaScript from the pinned snapshot, with isolated in-memory saves; they did not operate on a player’s browser save.

One climbing road, one visual world

Retain the upward road, planet nodes, current-pilot marker, independent star pips and the reward rail. Replace the single all-purpose background and globally rotated planet bank with each zone’s visual family. The environment owns the palette, painted scene, map planet choices and decorative debris. The live game continues to own the collision objects.

ElementConcrete behavior
Continuous sceneryAt a boundary after position b, blend over four mission spacings, from b−1.5 to b+2.5. Use a smooth blend of adjacent painted plates and color washes; stagger distant forms and debris so there is no horizontal seam. The road stroke and node spacing continue uninterrupted.
Names, not chaptersUse a quiet place-name label near an established scenic landmark and a small current-zone name in the header. No zone number, zone completion counter, tabs, unlock wall or ten-node frame. Mission detail still shows its global level number and name.
Planets and debrisMap nodes select deterministically from that zone’s planetBias. Decorative debris uses its debrisBias. Freeze map-art choices by mission ID so rewards or reordering do not shuffle the scenery. Keep foreground collision art/size intact; reject map combinations that obscure the number or pips.
Barrier treatmentOnly the three intentional Hyper Run rubble bands cross the road. Color their rubble to the surrounding zone, preserve the time label and arrival state, and keep reward markers clear of each band. Background decoration never creates a fourth apparent blockage.
NavigationOpen at the earliest unlocked incomplete mission, or at the blocking barrier when that is the next action. Add Return to pilot and Find level by number/name. A compact place-name locator scrolls the same road; it does not switch pages or bypass locks. Restore the last mission anchor and local offset when closing a detail sheet.
Growth and completionUse ordered mission IDs to resolve previous/next. At the published end, show “Current chart complete” plus a quiet continuation into space. Do not create fake locked nodes. Preserve earned edition titles when new missions are added.
Long-map performanceThe current 92-pixel spacing would make 260 nodes about 23,982 pixels tall. Render the visible window plus overscan, targeting at most 48 active node canvases and nearby reward art. Keep the logical road intact; load only current/neighbor scenery. Do not allocate one full-height raster background.
Mobile and accessCheck 320/390-pixel portrait and wide landscape. Minimum 44-pixel hit targets; readable numbers/stars on every palette; do not rely on color alone. Keyboard/focus navigation can reach off-window nodes by mounting the target. Honor reduced motion and the saved motion preference.
Reward railGroup rewards sharing a star threshold into one expandable marker. Label each with its star requirement; its map position is the earliest possible earning position, not a reward for finishing that level. Keep a pinned next-reward readout accurate for one-star players.

Zone remaster: painted depth plus procedural stars

Use the current Spill panorama as the material, depth and readability reference: painterly surfaces, distant structures at the borders, warm acorn/bronze accents, cool space depth, and a quiet central flight region. The goal is 26 recognizable places in the same illustrated universe, not 26 unrelated art styles.

Shared composition: dark base → painted distant scene → restrained environmental wash/scrim → procedural depth stars → live planets/debris/pickups → player and HUD. Star movement and background pan are cosmetic and use a separate visual RNG. Use continuous low-amplitude twinkle, never a full-screen flash or tap-linked opacity change. Gameplay and map crops read one ZoneVisual record.

Deliverables per zone: one wide painted master with the main flight area clear, an approved portrait crop anchor, a compact map crop and explicit color/contrast metadata. Start with a 3:1 master at roughly 3072 × 1024; a larger source is acceptable. Use a runtime dark treatment for Deep/Lost only if it passes comparison against their current restrained look; otherwise provide a dedicated dark derivative from the same composition. These are visual variants, not additional zone identities.

Existing behavior to retain: Deep/Lost keep their dark plate character and subtle wash; Arcade keeps its retro painter; Spill keeps its current sector/depot artwork and wave behavior. Prismwing’s existing procedural color effect must remain available on the procedural layer/wash; do not hue-rotate painted scenery or remove an earned pal effect. Honor the existing motion controls. No baked-in pilot, collectible, sharp foreground obstruction, HUD lettering, fake interactable or route cue belongs in a background.

Asset routing: add stable zone keys and a manifest of painted/map/dark assets, palette, crop anchor and a fixed visual seed. The existing procedural sky currently wins the fallback chain, so hybrid composition must be explicit in drawBackdrop and use the same lookup on both pages. Keep a procedural-only fallback for loading failures. Lazy-load the current and adjacent zone; target about 300 KB per delivered panorama and at most four full decoded plates in the working cache, then measure real devices before fixing the budget. Bump ART_VER and regenerate output when approved art lands.

Readability must be measured again: update sky color/luminance metadata from the final composite and assess the real planet/debris families at phone size. The current free planet-selection contrast loop consumes random draws; separate visual selection from authored route RNG so a color correction cannot alter gate positions or a mission seed. Preserve registered sprite dimensions and collision radii. More detail belongs mostly outside the player’s immediate route.

The Spill’s existing BLACKOUT is a gradual dimming veil with hazard outlines, not the tap-triggered strobe. Preserve that wave modifier while removing the Star Map flash behavior. The two draw paths carrying the campaign strobe and the mission strobe timer/copy must be retired together after approval; a low-motion preference must not be required to avoid it.

Complete 260-mission manifest

Every entry has an immutable ID, explicit target, all three objectives, numeric modifiers, a duration target, a challenge brief and a distinction from both neighbors. Expand a zone to inspect its ten entries. Internal grouping here is for review only; the player-facing map is continuous.

Duration: these are active successful-flight design targets, not new timers or claimed playtest measurements. Existing flight targets are estimates around the retained gate counts. Spill ranges derive from its current spawning/countdown/docking windows with up to six seconds of drain per wave; they exclude untimed Depot choices, pauses and recovery. Spill finish targets and seeds are explicit frozen values, never calculated from the proposed zone number.

Tuning: pace/width/sway/rate are multipliers, fog is the existing continuous fog value. New missions keep at least four spare ordinary-acorn opportunities and use existing goldNeeded+one-spare planning. A no-shield goal means no shield spent; “no hull damage” does not mean no protected contact. Pal effects, owned shields and mission mod suppression retain current rules. Durations are calibrated on a neutral loadout, and existing pal effects must be tested rather than assumed disabled.

Rewards without moving earned goalposts

Retain every existing threshold and entitlement. The 53 functional rungs stay where they are; the nine obsolete “chapter opened” rows are documentation/UI claims, not real entitlements, and leave the progression UI. The Cat Suit and STARLORD stay at 300. GATECRASHER stays at 250. Reword “every star” to “300-star milestone” so the expansion does not promise the wrong requirement.

Reveal, purchase and ownership remain distinct. Existing star-gated helmets/suits retain their current prices and unlock/reveal behavior; trails and pals retain their existing grant/equip rules. Start Shield still unlocks arming at 6 stars and costs 25 acorns per charge; Shield Battery stays at 27. Preserve all previously owned/bought items even if a later catalog hides their shelf. Do not make an existing premium item a new reward placeholder.

Spill asset discipline: ship skins retain the 58-logical-pixel ship length, the current collision radius, cockpit/pilot anchors, canopy opening, upgrade silhouettes and the four modular tracks. Apply a material treatment across the existing tier parts rather than drawing a new ship with a different flight body. Trails reuse the existing plume/particle motion; appearance trims are static. Pals reuse the existing companion animation/placement approach but have no magnet, shield, scanner, damage, Ore or speed effect. They must not cover hazards or impersonate a protective effect.

Selection and persistence: store cosmetic IDs in separate Spill appearance preferences and an entitlement list; do not reuse gameplay upgrade or utility IDs. Cosmetics may accompany a mission without changing its standard ship stats, seed or zero starting utility configuration. Use the same painter in flight, Depot and Loadout. A missing cosmetic asset falls back to the standard visible ship and keeps ownership. Sample placeholders are clearly labeled in review. For a live rung whose art is delayed, preserve a stable reserved entitlement, show that it is awaiting art, and make it equip-ready when the asset arrives; do not silently substitute a different reward.

Explicit identity and save migration

Recommended model: immutable mission ID → immutable objective contract and explicit seed; a separate ordered list supplies display positions. Keep the existing strings “1-1” through “10-10” as opaque identities, not formulas. Every new ID and seed is listed in the manifest. Future name changes do not rename an ID. Future reordering changes only the order list; a changed objective needs a new objective ID/contract and an explicit migration decision.

RecordMapping / behavior
Production saveKeep acornaut_illust_v1. Add a versioned campaign namespace; do not change SAVE_KEY. Retain the original raw stars map and a pre-migration snapshot until recovery is verified.
Beta saveKeep acornaut_illust_beta. Read and record whether its first seed came from production or a legacy key; migrate only the beta slot. Never write beta grants, skips or experiment results into production.
Old mission identity/orderFor every a-b ID with a=1..10 and b=1..10, retain that exact ID and displayOrder=(a−1)×10+b. The full 100-row mapping below is explicit. New positions 101–260 have no old mission or earned objective to copy.
Known compatible objectivesCopy each of the three bits to the corresponding immutable objective ID only where its goal meaning, threshold, base and finish target are established as compatible. Replays OR successful objective records. Changing only the strobe presentation leaves the objective definitions intact.
Unversioned changed objectivesProduction N-8, N=2..10, and beta N-4 / N-8 have ambiguous prior contracts. Preserve the raw mask, star count and legacy passage. Do not assert current Ore, no-hit, Flow or wave-20 goals from it. Label these carried stars as earlier credit on detail/results; current objective ticks require a successful current-contract run.
Star count for ambiguous entriesFor one mission, creditedStars=max(legacyCreditCount, popcount(verifiedCurrentMask)). Verified current goals union independently across successful replays. This keeps old credit, never marks a different goal as earned, never double-pays for old credit, and never exceeds three stars per mission.
Route completion for ambiguous entriesIf the old finish bit is set, preserve routePassage for that existing ID. It continues to open the next mission, even if its current-mode objective checklist is unverified. Side-star-only masks do not create passage. Passage credit does not create a Spill wave clear, mastery award or new finish record.
Unknown/invalid source keysKeep their raw values in the migration snapshot; do not attach them to a new mission. Use only the three bits that current countBits recognized when recording legacy credit. Preserve the pre-migration entitlement floor and all owned rewards; surface unsupported provenance for review instead of inventing objective history.
raceGates33 → hyper-barrier-1 (after 33); 66 → hyper-barrier-2 (after 66); 99 → hyper-barrier-3 (after 99). Retain the numeric compatibility array. Preserve all existing clears, including out-of-order/early ones. Never infer a missing clear from star totals or a best race time.
Hyper Run mode entitlementExisting clear 33 retains access; beta still bypasses. Store the earned access fact independently if a future relocation is approved. raceRecords[hyper-run] remains unchanged; legacy prototype records already deleted by older builds cannot be reconstructed.
Spill fixed mission seedsKeep 5018, 5028, 5038, 5048, 5058, 5068, 5078, 5088 and 5098 with their original IDs. Do not derive from new display order, new zone index or cosmetic seed.
Beta Wormhole seedsKeep 7014, 7024, 7034, 7044, 7054, 7064, 7074, 7084 and 7094. Record distinct beta-tunnel-N-4 variant IDs so a beta goal is never a production goal. They occupy existing beta positions; they do not add campaign star slots.
Ordinary legacy flight seedsNo fixed mission seed exists in current main for Normal/Deep/Lost/Arcade. Preserve seed=null and the legacy random route behavior; do not pretend a previous course can be recovered. New missions use the explicit 32-bit seeds in the manifest and a versioned scoped generator.
New seeded flightThe manifest freezes each seed once (derived for this draft from the immutable ID using SHA-256, first 32 bits; the checked-in integer is authoritative). Implement a scoped, versioned PRNG for route choices and a separate visual stream. Never replace global Math.random or allow background stars, resize, load order or art rejection loops to consume route randomness. Compare repeatability at identical viewport/input; cross-viewport flight geometry is not claimed identical.
Wallet and purchased/owned listsCopy acorns, starDust, purchased, unlocked suits/helmets/trails/pals and equipped preferences. Snapshot all existing threshold-based entitlements too, including items not yet equipped. New reveal code must accept previously owned or purchased items before a threshold check.
Dust ledgerGive each legacy dust rung a stable reward ID. Mark every rung at or below dustPaidTo as paid; do not pay it again. Settle only genuinely unpaid legacy backlog up to the prior eligible total. Keep dustPaidTo as a compatibility high-water mark. New rewards settle once by reward ID, in one save transaction.
Titles and CatKeep Cat eligibility/ownership at 300 and STARLORD at 300; retain GATECRASHER at 250 and all lower titles. New title collection is additive. No re-price or refund is assumed.
allStarsPreserve the flag and legacy entitlement floor of 300. Recommended effective reward count is max(earned credited total, 300 when flagged); display actual earned/credited route progress separately. Main does not let this flag bypass sequential mission/barrier checks; do not claim it did. Expanding the override to all future rewards requires a separate choice.
zonesSeenMap each existing exact ENVS.name to its stable zone ID; deduplicate and preserve unknown names. Backfill a fixed-zone visit only from supported evidence: a compatible completed flight mission or a verified current-contract first-play record. Do not infer visits from unplayed unlocked zones, beta accessibility, map scrolling, an ambiguous swapped mission, or a Spill mission whose painter never visited that zone.
Spill progression and checkpointCopy spillBest, spillRecords, spillSuspended, starter/signal and all checkpoint ledger/RNG fields unchanged. Existing records remain authoritative for first-pass state. A migrated star for 10-8 must not manufacture spillBest=20, expeditions, utilities or a first-pass celebration.
Idempotence and interruptionRun a pure migration in memory, retain source-slot/version provenance, validate it, then write the new namespace atomically with a raw backup. A repeat load must make no new grant. If snapshot/write fails, keep the old save usable; do not partially move or clear it.
Release coexistenceThe migration preserves raw legacy progress for recovery; it does not promise that an older app bundle understands the new namespace. Do not allow an old tab to overwrite a newer campaign version silently. Detect and reload a stale writer; do not downgrade saves.

Example of honest carried credit: an unversioned production save has stars[“2-8”]=7 but no matching Spill record. It keeps three credited stars and passage past position 18. Its current four-wave / 41-Ore / no-hull-damage checklist is unverified. A successful current replay can certify those objectives without adding another three rewards. An old 10-8 finish similarly cannot prove a wave-20 milestone.

This treatment is a proposed decision, not a claim that provenance can be recovered. If the owner prefers a different presentation for carried stars, that can change; the underlying requirements remain no loss, no double counting, and no newly asserted objective from an unrelated old bit.

The pre-migration entitlement floor for unknown or unsupported keys applies only to the legacy reward set. It does not manufacture new mission stars or unlock the proposed extension. Future reward eligibility uses credited stars on recognized active route missions, while previously owned items and legacy eligibility stay permanent.

All existing missions: explicit mapping

C = compatible unchanged objective mapping, subject to supported source history. L = preserve raw mask/credit/passage with unverified objective provenance. For any older save whose source contract cannot be established beyond the known collision list, use L rather than guessing. A no-flash retune changes presentation, not the listed objective definitions.

Bounded implementation, starting with 30 levels

The first content sample is Deep Space 1–10, Rust Belt 101–110, and Blackout Zone 241–250. This deliberately samples onboarding, salvage-themed mid-route precision and late low-visibility flight without pretending those zones are adjacent. It contains ten preserved onboarding missions and twenty new missions. The Blackout sample replaces darkness-as-flashing with steady fog and existing control modifiers.

The phase also removes strobe from the ten existing affected flight configurations because that is now an explicit user requirement. That is a global presentation/config correction, not ten additional new authored missions. The nine Spill missions remain untouched.

Stage after approvalBounded deliverableExit condition
1. Isolated baselineFetch main again; inspect new PRs; create an isolated branch from the then-current main (suggested codex/star-map-sample). Record any baseline changes before touching game files. Check in the approved specification and explicit manifest contracts.No existing working tree is repurposed; baseline and scope are reviewable.
2. Progress foundationStable mission/zone/variant IDs; separate order; explicit legacy seeds; versioned progress/entitlement ledger; data-derived counts and next/previous lookup; honest roadmap generation. Fix guaranteed pickups and record zone visits.All legacy progress fixtures preserve stars, passage, barriers, prices, rewards, saves and Spill checkpoint content.
3. Three visual mastersCreate/remaster Deep Space, Rust Belt and Blackout Zone using the Spill quality reference. Integrate painted + procedural-star composition into map and relevant gameplay views; include portrait/landscape crop proof and no-flash samples.Owner can review the actual art at phone size, including planets/debris/pilot/HUD and transition seams. Failed loads remain playable.
4. Thirty-mission sampleImplement only the twenty new sample definitions plus the ten preserved onboarding missions as the review set. Explicit seeds, goals and modifier rows are those above; tune only with recorded reasons. Add clear beta sample navigation that launches canonical IDs in isolated preview progress.All 30 can be inspected/replayed; no experimental stars or grants leak into normal production progress.
5. Small reward proofPrototype Rust Wake and Rust Runner in the existing Spill painter plus one clearly labeled Rivet placeholder preview. Show flight/Depot/Loadout and every upgrade state needed to prove layering. Keep the rest of the reward extension data-only.Cosmetics change no state in the Spill simulation or checkpoint ledger; original pilot/helmet fits and upgrade silhouettes remain.
6. Review PRRun production and beta acceptance separately. Generate shipping docs output through the repo pipeline, include a short change/reward/migration report and known playtest limitations, and open a PR for owner review.Do not merge or deploy. The first PR remains a sample, with production expansion disabled.
7. Later accepted batchesAfter the sample direction is accepted: author/integrate remaining zones in groups of at most four (40 missions). The final group can be smaller. Reuse the proven migration/compositor. Assemble the final 260-level active order only after required mission/art acceptance.No blanket late-game length scaling and no new Spill mission generator. Final activation is a separately reviewable PR decision.

Production versus preview: the first sample PR keeps the normal published route at 100 missions / 300 stars. It may carry the compatible fixes and accepted remaster infrastructure, but new sample results live in a separate preview namespace. A beta “sample route” is a testing locator, not a shortened production road: 101–110 and 241–250 retain their proposed positions/IDs. Exercise the entire 260-node map with draft nodes clearly labeled and inactive outside the sample; do not present unimplemented routes as playable. Final activation uses the same production predicates, not beta unlock bypasses.

Release manifest: keep published mission order, published reward IDs and preview content separate. The sample build’s normal production and beta campaign each retain their current 100 positions and 53 functional reward rungs; only the isolated review surface exposes the new sample content. Do not make the hub show an unreachable 780-star denominator or a future reward as though the expansion were already live. Final activation publishes the 260-position order and approved new reward IDs together.

New-route RNG contract: use a scoped Mulberry32 stream seeded by the explicit manifest integer, with each advance adding 0x6D2B79F5 modulo 2³² and the standard integer-multiply/xor mixing. Freeze the generator and its consumption order under flight-seeded-v1, with a known-output fixture. Route geometry, gameplay pickup decisions and orientation phases use this stream; painted-star placement and sprite-family choices use independent visual streams. Legacy missions continue using their existing random route path, and Spill/Wormhole/Hyper Run keep their existing generators.

campaign.ts + explicit manifest dataReplace stage generation as the source of new content with immutable mission records and an ordered route. Retain compatibility exports where necessary. Store all goals, seeds and no-flash replacements explicitly.
catalog.tsStable environment IDs/visual records; retain ENVS index order and existing prices; preserve all old thresholds; append approved cosmetic reward identifiers.
standalone.tsVirtualized continuous road, visual-family nodes, subtle place names, navigation, goal/credit labeling, actual-order next buttons, derived totals and honest reward/completion wording.

save.tsVersioned migration, provenance, objective records, legacy passage/credit, owned-entitlement union, stable reward IDs, separate beta preview saves and Spill cosmetic preferences.
engine.tsCanonical launch/order checks, fixed seed injection, idempotent reward settlement, optional accepted barrier arrival correction, shared cosmetic preferences. Keep Spill resume and first-pass banking intact.
draw.ts / art.ts / sky-gen.tsHybrid zone compositor and bounded lazy loading; shared zone metadata; remove both campaign strobe paint paths; preserve the Spill painter’s simulation contract and legacy procedural pal appearance.

Acceptance before a PR is presented as ready

The following are implementation gates, not tests already passed by this document. The manifest itself has already been checked for 260 unique IDs, complete order 1–260, 26 distinct catalog environments with ten entries each, 780 objective slots, zero strobe flags, exactly three unchanged barriers, 30 sample entries, 160 unique new seeds, and unchanged modes/targets/objectives for the original 100 missions.

AreaRequired evidence
Production progressionFresh save: only First Solo available. A one-star pass advances every position including 10→11, 99→100, 100→101 and 259→260 in the final active manifest; stops occur only at the three uncleared barriers. Star totals cannot skip a prerequisite. Existing completed missions remain replayable.
Barrier boundariesAt 33, 66 and 99 verify arrival, earlier-clear requirements, launch/refusal, a time exactly at the limit and one tick too slow. A zero/negative clock never clears. One race never clears more than one barrier. If arrival correction is approved, ordinary mode replays cannot bank an unreached future barrier. Existing clears and mode access survive migration.
Independent starsSuccessful runs earning different side goals union correctly; failure adds none; replay adds no duplicate credit/Dust. A carried old mask never certifies a current Ore/Flow/no-hit/wave-20 objective. All ambiguous-credit combinations stay at 0–3 credited stars per slot and never reduce the imported count.
Migration fixture coverageFresh, partial, complete 300-star, noncontiguous legacy progress, masks with side stars but no finish, allStars, bought Cat/premium, threshold-unlocked-but-never-equipped items, every barrier subset, old dustPaidTo, unknown IDs, pre-Spill production, old beta seconds/score Spill, twelve-wave 10-8, production-seeded beta, and current Depot checkpoints. Run migration twice and simulate write interruption.
Mission identity / seedReshuffle display order in a fixture and show each fixed Spill/Wormhole seed is unchanged. Restart the same new flight seed with identical inputs/viewport and compare route data. Change art loading, map scroll, reward rendering and visual RNG without changing its route. Legacy ordinary flight remains explicitly unseeded.
Pickup feasibilityFor every distinct goal budget in the sample and worst-case approved combinations, verify all promised plain/gold pickups exist, are legible and reachable with spare opportunities; include Bee and gold overlap. Optional rolls cannot consume guaranteed slots. Do not certify every full-game route from a single bot result.
Zone visitsOpening a briefing/map is not a visit. First actual play in a fixed zone records it once; transition visits and reloads stay idempotent. Backfill does not create visits from ambiguous mission bits or from beta unlock flags.
Spill invariantsExisting missions remain 4/5/6/7/8/9/10/11/20 waves on seeds 5018…5098, with the exact Ore/no-hull-damage goals. Standard mission utilities stay empty. Ordinary mode continues after wave 20 with the same build. First-pass celebration remains once; later wave-20 Depots stay ordinary. Leave a Depot open for an hour; checkpoint/reload never duplicates records, Ore or rewards.
Visual remasterCompare map/gameplay crops at 320 and 390 portrait, tablet and landscape. Show all three sample palettes, adjacent-zone blends, full/failed asset loading, near white/dark hazard families, pilot/helmet readability, current procedural pal effects, reduced motion and continuous Blackout visibility. Decorative scenery must not resemble collision threats in the route.
Spill cosmeticsCompare each approved appearance across the current 192 modular ship configurations; preserve canopy masks/pilot anchors and module tier readability. Render in flight, Depot and Loadout. Cosmetic selection, trail or pal must not alter seed, physics, utility slots, Ore, hull or first-pass records.
Map scale / betaRender 260 nodes and a synthetic 300-node future extension without fixed 100/300 limits, misplaced barriers or inaccessible focus targets. Return-to-pilot, locked-barrier focus, search and restored anchors work. Beta’s existing nine tunnel variants and save slot remain distinct; repeat all critical lock checks with the beta flag absent.
Required repo outputsUse the repository TypeScript/export and roadmap pipeline only after implementation approval. Run affected progression, Hyper Run, Spill, HUD/continue and art checks; record baseline failures separately. Compare generated production and beta loaders to the source, run diff checks, and give the owner the PR without merge/deploy.

Difficulty acceptance is still open: the numeric rows make the proposal implementable, but playtest determines whether neighboring missions feel distinct and fair. Review successful active duration, first-star completion, collectible opportunity and repeated-failure points in the 30-level sample. Keep the short relief missions. Adjust named rows with a changelog; do not use zone number as a hidden difficulty or length formula. No new gameplay analytics service is required.

Next authorized action is review. Approving the first sample can authorize the isolated branch, foundation, three remastered zones, twenty new sample missions, no-flash corrections and small Spill cosmetic proof. It does not implicitly approve barrier relocation, all 26 finished art sets, final 260-route activation, merge or deployment.
